checks: For d≥2 the predecessor boundary calculation applies to exactly the defined uniform barycentric law. With d positive entries, the cap volume is at most t^d divided by the product of those entries, with equality at small t. For k<d positive entries it is at least a positive multiple of t^k near zero, giving capacity zero, and for the all-zero row the ratio equals t. For d=1 the single nonzero coordinate is uniform on [0,b] after scaling and the capacity is exactly b.

Discarding zero-capacity rows retains only rows whose unique zero is fixed within each group. The chosen maximal nonnegative weight times the geometric mean of the sum dominates the old weighted sum by superadditivity. This includes a group whose largest weight is zero.

Surviving labels are distinct and have distinct zero columns, so their prescribed diagonal zeros define an injective partial permutation of columns. Non-surviving rows are zero at this stage. Merging preserved the retained column masses, which were at most one, so after the permutation each remaining budget is nonnegative and can be filled in an off-diagonal position because d+1≥2.

Filling column budgets preserves all diagonal zeros and raises entries only, hence no row mean decreases. The new vector of row means is a feasible member of D_d. Repeating for arbitrary c≥0 proves the support bound. Nonnegative separation then gives one admissible coordinatewise dominator even though the weight-by-weight constructions can differ.
